scenarios.when: the current host uses a Pure Tokens connection and the user asks to generate, create, draw, or edit an image without naming a Skill
scenarios.then: select puretokens-image before generic imagegen, Imagen, or another image Skill. Once selected, use only the fixed Images API path; a missing executor, rejection, or failure must stop safely and must not invoke a generic media Skill.

scenarios.when: A command for the bound host returns an active_connection_*, workbuddy_*, or host_credential_adapter_unavailable local failure, including when the user asks to continue generation.
scenarios.then: Stop the automatic API flow. Do not invoke connection, init, doctor, models, another Skill, or another --host as a recovery probe. Preserve the original request and any existing task ID; never resubmit automatically. Explain only that this invocation sent no API request. An explicit recheck request or verified new diagnostic evidence permits one relevant check on the same host; changing host requires explicit user selection.

scenarios.when: an alias resolves to multiple exact model IDs
scenarios.then: ask the user to choose an exact ID; do not submit

scenarios.when: a user asks for text-to-image with the default model, a uniquely resolved installed alias, or an exact model ID using only known core fields
scenarios.then: submit directly without reading /v1/media/models first

scenarios.when: validation, submission, task-status, or content delivery fails
scenarios.then: return failure_phase, api_error_code only when the public API explicitly returned that exact code and omit it otherwise, HTTP status only when returned, a sanitized user-facing error message, and an actionable next step; include retry_after_seconds when the executor returns a valid positive Retry-After and never expose raw response bodies, upstream identifiers, internal URLs, stacks, request data, credentials, or user media

scenarios.when: a terminal failure has an explicit public API code content_moderation or sanitized public API detail that unambiguously says the request did not pass safety review
scenarios.then: tell the user the image was not generated because it did not pass safety review, suggest adjusting the prompt or reference media, do not invent an API code when none was returned, and never retry automatically

scenarios.when: the user provides a current image URL or attachment but does not state whether it is a visual reference or the image to edit
scenarios.then: ask the user to choose reference or edit before a billable submission; do not infer a role from the file, URL, or model name

scenarios.when: the user asks for a poster, cover, illustration, or other visual design without explicitly requesting maps, geographic research, workspace/history search, or a quality review
scenarios.then: treat it as the stated visual-design task only; do not invoke unrelated Skills, search prior conversations or files, inspect old media, or extend the task with compliance or research work

scenarios.when: one request contains multiple distinct image briefs or assets
scenarios.then: do not map the briefs to n, split the request into multiple billable submissions, or silently drop an item; ask the user to choose the first asset for this request

scenarios.when: preparing a text-to-image, reference-image, or edit prompt
scenarios.then: preserve explicit purpose, subject, scene, style, composition, verbatim text, and constraints; only add intent-preserving detail to an underspecified request, identify each input image role, and do not invent brands, subjects, copy, or a different operation

scenarios.when: User explicitly requests an image and then a video using that generated image as its first frame.
scenarios.then: Read the bounded workflow guide and both selected profiles. Confirm declared local-byte first-frame transport before generating the image, without network preflights. Deliver the selected image index before passing its unchanged verified local file to video. Keep separate records; unsupported inputs, uncertain submission or downstream failure stop the chain without repeating the image or silently substituting a URL/text prompt.

scenarios.when: the Images API explicitly rejects a model, parameter, or capability and returns no task ID
scenarios.then: read the catalog at most once for diagnosis, show returned current candidates or allowed values, and require an explicit corrected new request; never resubmit automatically

scenarios.when: the Images API returns 429 before a task ID is confirmed
scenarios.then: report Retry-After when returned, ask the user to wait and explicitly retry, and do not poll, wait, or retry automatically

scenarios.when: a submission has a 5xx response, transport error, or timeout before a task ID is confirmed
scenarios.then: state that task acceptance is unknown, do not claim the task was not created, and never automatically resubmit

scenarios.when: the managed native executor returns a parseable sanitized failure
scenarios.then: Preserve the native command, failure phase, submission_outcome and available task context. For submit, validation confirms no POST; transmission/submission uncertainty never authorizes repetition. For status, wait, resume or content, validation means that command failed locally and says nothing about whether the already known task exists. Keep its ID and correct only the local continuation request.

scenarios.when: the host blocks the API request before it starts because of system policy, approval policy, or external-network execution permission
scenarios.then: return failure_phase validation with task_id, http_status, and api_error_code all not returned; state that the Images API did not execute and no image task was created; do not call it submission, claim charging, refunding, or API rejection, or repeat POST. Tell the user to retry only in a host session that allows external network requests and approval of that operation; never claim the Skill can request, elevate, or bypass host permissions.

scenarios.when: the user requests an image, visual reference, or image edit
scenarios.then: invoke the installed managed native executor with the current host ID and the declared fixed Images API request. For a current attachment and declared image_edit operation, give it only that exact multipart attachment path; never invoke Imagen, another media Skill, a browser, Switch, Desktop, or Computer Use.

scenarios.when: the executor cannot start or confirms a credential, parameter or attachment-preparation failure before the media POST begins
scenarios.then: Preserve the native receipt phase. Only a confirmed pre-POST validation failure means no media task was submitted. Attachment/network transmission failures after POST may have started are unknown submissions; retain any task ID and never automatically resubmit or use another transport.

scenarios.when: the executor POST started but returns an execution error, empty output, truncated output, or output that cannot be parsed before a task ID is confirmed
scenarios.then: treat submission acceptance as unknown and do not invoke POST again, submit a replacement task, or claim the task was not created, charged, or refunded. If no verified task_id is available, return one unknown-submission receipt and end the current response after only local cleanup of this temporary request file; no further API, status, polling or submission work.

scenarios.when: a later user message says continue, retry, or similar but supplies no verified task ID for an earlier unknown submission
scenarios.then: state that the original task cannot be continued, ask the user to explicitly confirm a new paid image request, and do not submit until that confirmation arrives in a new user turn.

scenarios.when: an on-demand live catalog read, used only for an installed-profile gap or post-rejection diagnosis, lacks the exact requested image ID or capability
scenarios.then: state that the current authenticated connection did not return the exact model, list returned catalog candidates, and do not resubmit or switch models. If the user expects access, direct them to the Pure Tokens client configuration to select a group that contains that exact model, create or select a managed key covering the selected groups, verify and apply it to the current host, then start a new host conversation and explicitly retry. Do not claim which group contains the model unless an authenticated API response explicitly returned that mapping.

scenarios.when: the installed index/selected profile and any permitted one-time on-demand catalog read have no schema for a requested n, size, image_size, aspect ratio, reference field, or other optional parameter
scenarios.then: explain that the model parameter profile is not published, ask the user to remove that option or choose a model with an explicit profile, and do not submit that unverified option

scenarios.when: a requested optional parameter is absent from the installed or on-demand schema, or its value violates the declared enum or range
scenarios.then: list the profile-supported values and ask the user to choose one; do not submit

scenarios.when: the exact image profile declares requires_together or size_expression_precedence constraints and the user supplies width, height, aspect ratio, or size
scenarios.then: require every declared companion field such as width plus height. When more than one declared size expression is supplied, send only the highest-precedence user-supplied expression, state that expression in the receipt, and never mix lower-precedence fields.

scenarios.when: a one-time live catalog read is needed for an explicit unsupported option, media operation, or diagnosis but fails
scenarios.then: report that read failure; do not let it block a normal core text-to-image submission, and do not retry or resubmit automatically

scenarios.when: a direct fixed-Pure-Tokens API request fails before task acceptance or native image bytes cannot be handed off
scenarios.then: report the returned failure or delivery state, state whether a task_id was returned, and do not guess a configuration cause or submit a replacement task

scenarios.when: the requested count is not allowed by the selected model profile's properties.n
scenarios.then: explain the one-task limit, list the profile-declared count values or range, and ask for a supported count; do not submit

scenarios.when: a requested pixel canvas, semantic image size, aspect ratio, or other image parameter is not declared by the exact authenticated model profile
scenarios.then: list the profile-declared options for that field and ask the user to choose one; do not submit

scenarios.when: the request uses a physical dimension such as 200cm x 230cm
scenarios.then: explain that physical dimensions cannot be guaranteed and ask for a supported pixel canvas; do not submit

scenarios.when: the user attaches an image and the installed or permitted on-demand profile has no compatible image_edit operation
scenarios.then: state that this exact model has not published native image-attachment capability and do not submit or switch models

scenarios.when: the user provides a public reference-image URL but the installed or permitted on-demand profile lacks a matching property and declared public-URL reference transport
scenarios.then: state that the selected model has not published a compatible public-URL reference field, list any declared reference fields, and do not submit or switch models

scenarios.when: the user asks to edit a public image URL but the installed profile and permitted one-time on-demand catalog read lack an image_edit operation with application/json, an exact public-URL field, and declared public-URL transport
scenarios.then: state that the selected model has not published public-URL editing; if it has only a reference field, ask whether the user wants a new image using it as a reference, and do not downgrade or submit without explicit confirmation

scenarios.when: the user provides a reference-image URL that is not a public HTTPS URL
scenarios.then: explain that the selected profile requires a public HTTPS URL and ask the user to provide one; do not submit

scenarios.when: a reference URL contains credentials, localhost, a .local host, or an explicit loopback, private, or link-local IP
scenarios.then: reject it as non-public without DNS lookup or probing and ask for a public HTTPS URL; do not submit

scenarios.when: more than one declared public-URL reference field could represent the user's request
scenarios.then: list the declared fields and ask the user to choose the intended input mode; do not guess or submit

scenarios.when: the user designates a current local native image attachment as a visual reference and the selected profile declares image_edit multipart_file input
scenarios.then: use that exact declared image_edit operation, path, fields, and count limits in one direct Images API request. Preserve the user's reference intent in the prompt; do not upload, rehost, create a URL, or silently turn it into text-only generation.

scenarios.when: the user designates a current local native image attachment as a visual reference but the selected profile has no image_edit multipart_file operation, the attachment count is outside its declared range, or the host cannot hand off its bytes
scenarios.then: stop before POST and ask for a public HTTPS URL for that image, or an explicit new text-only request that ignores the attachment. Do not inspect, describe, summarize, transcribe, recreate, or infer from the attachment for a text-to-image prompt; do not upload it, make a URL, search historical images, or silently downgrade.

scenarios.when: an image-edit profile requires multipart_file but the current host cannot send the user's explicit attachment bytes with the direct API request
scenarios.then: stop before submission, explain that attachment-byte delivery is unavailable, and do not read credentials, create a URL, or downgrade to text-to-image

scenarios.when: the current host can send the user's current multipart image attachment through the declared Images API operation for a visual reference or explicit edit
scenarios.then: send it only with that single direct Images API request; do not call a separate upload path or expose internal attachment handling

scenarios.when: an edit request includes a mask, multiple references, or another field not explicitly declared by the installed or permitted on-demand image_edit profile
scenarios.then: list the declared operation limits and ask the user to adjust the request; do not submit

scenarios.when: a submission returns a valid top-level task_id, or top-level id when task_id is absent
scenarios.then: Use the executor-returned task_id unchanged, including dots in model labels and colons in legacy output IDs. Supported IDs have length 1..256: an ASCII letter, digit, underscore or hyphen first, then those characters plus dots and colons. Reject paths, encoded input, whitespace and control characters. Never derive an ID from URLs or nested data or parse its model hint.

scenarios.when: a submission response has no supported top-level task_id or id
scenarios.then: report that task_id was not returned and cannot be safely continued; do not derive one from URLs or nested data, poll, download, or resubmit

scenarios.when: a continuation request provides a URL, multiple IDs, or an empty task ID
scenarios.then: ask for exactly one opaque task ID and do not extract, concatenate, or query an ID

scenarios.when: the executor returns status unknown for an unsupported API status
scenarios.then: Report that the state could not be classified, retain the task ID, stop automatic polling and require an explicit same-task continuation. Do not seek or display the raw API state.

scenarios.when: a same-task status response contains reconciliation_required: true regardless of its status value
scenarios.then: treat it as a terminal operational outcome: stop ordinary polling, retain the same task_id, report that status verification is required, and do not resubmit, switch models, infer a refund, or expose provider or billing details

scenarios.when: a task continuation has no trustworthy original requested n
scenarios.then: ask the user for the original image count before content delivery; do not guess indexes or report partial delivery as complete

scenarios.when: the same task is in a supported pending state
scenarios.then: report the current state and continue reading only that task

scenarios.when: the same task is in a supported pending state
scenarios.then: for a newly accepted pending image without API Retry-After, submit emits retry_not_before 5 seconds after the accepted response. Carry that exact timestamp across tool handoff/records; wait only its remaining delay, then query every 3 seconds. An absent or expired timestamp permits an immediate first read. API Retry-After takes precedence; never restart the initial delay on continuation. Stop at 40 same-task reads or the 120-second window including network and wait time

scenarios.when: a same-task status request returns HTTP 429
scenarios.then: when a valid positive Retry-After fits the remaining automatic-polling budget, wait that duration and continue querying the same task; otherwise report the limit and stop this window; never submit a replacement task

scenarios.when: a task is in a supported pending state
scenarios.then: keep at most one same-task status request in flight, never create a background timer or queue, and stop automatic polling after a non-429 5xx response, transport error, or timeout

scenarios.when: the 120-second wait window or 40-read limit is exhausted, or the next wait cannot fit, and the same task is still in a supported pending state
scenarios.then: Return ok=true with supported pending status, wait_outcome and preserved wait_windows_completed. Only next_step=wait permits one more bounded foreground window while the authorized delivery remains active. At two completed windows or retry_deferred stop and offer explicit continuation. Never POST again.

scenarios.when: the user explicitly asks to continue querying the returned task_id
scenarios.then: Start one bounded same-task window on an explicit user request. Preserve the saturated wait_windows_completed counter; this does not reset automatic continuation permission. Never submit or substitute another task.

scenarios.when: the same task reports failure, cancellation, or expiry
scenarios.then: report the returned failure and require an explicit new request before another submission

scenarios.when: the status request times out or the submission outcome is unknown
scenarios.then: report the uncertainty, offer to continue querying the same task if an ID exists, and never auto-resubmit

scenarios.when: content retrieval fails before a verified local file is available
scenarios.then: Keep the task ID and offer only a same-task content retry when requested; never resubmit. If the download already succeeded and only host handoff failed, use completed-record resume to verify the existing file locally and reattach it without another content GET.

scenarios.when: native image bytes have been handed off after a completed task
scenarios.then: report an attachment or local path only when the current host actually confirms it; otherwise state that bytes were delivered through the current host and do not invent a preview, filename, or directory

scenarios.when: the requested image bytes have been successfully delivered for the current task
scenarios.then: return one completion receipt and end the current response. Do not automatically inspect quality, open the image, search workspace or conversation history, invoke another Skill, or create another media task; wait for a new explicit user request.

scenarios.when: a multi-image task has delivered some but not every requested zero-based content index from 0 through n-1
scenarios.then: report the delivered and missing indexes, offer only same-task retrieval for the missing indexes, and never resubmit

scenarios.when: a completed task has multiple image results
scenarios.then: read zero-based content indexes sequentially, hand off each native byte result before the next read, and do not prefetch, concurrently fetch, or re-fetch delivered content

scenarios.when: the user explicitly asks to check request parameters without generation
scenarios.then: invoke preflight once with the finite request file; it never POSTs. A required profile-gap catalog GET is allowed. Do not claim a price, funds, authorization or successful generation from validation.

scenarios.when: an explicit user/workspace task record is useful for later continuation
scenarios.then: pass its absolute path with submit --record. Keep only task identity, original operation, safe parameters and progress; no credentials, prompt or reference media. Resume only the recorded task and mark an index delivered only after actual host handoff.

scenarios.when: the user explicitly resumes a record with reconciliation_required true
scenarios.then: resume performs exactly one same-task status GET; keep the flag on failure or continued reconciliation, clear it only from the actual response, and use the returned status before further waiting or content retrieval; never POST

scenarios.when: the server returns an error containing request text, internal paths or an unknown code
scenarios.then: only use fixed executor category text, returned HTTP status and local next_action; omit unknown codes and arbitrary server error text, never guess the omitted reason

scenarios.when: downloaded or existing output has an invalid or truncated media container
scenarios.then: do not mark download or delivery successful, do not reuse or overwrite the corrupt file, retain the task and index and follow the safe same-task retrieval action

scenarios.when: content finds an existing valid media file without a matching explicit record download proof
scenarios.then: preserve the file; select another output directory and retrieve only this same task index; never claim reuse or submit a replacement

scenarios.when: a proposed recorded submission contains invalid free text in a structured parameter
scenarios.then: reject before creating the task record or sending POST; do not persist the free text

scenarios.when: ZCode has an enabled Pure Tokens connection but current conversation selection is not established
scenarios.then: do not infer routing from connection presence; require explicit host context or the user request naming Pure Tokens

scenarios.when: the current conversation model can respond and receives an independent API result or an explicit user question
scenarios.then: Only provide relevant user navigation: recognized insufficient quota/balance goes to https://console.puretokensx.com/wallet; explicit unanswerable spending-history questions go to https://console.puretokensx.com/usage-logs. A failure of the conversation model itself cannot be handled by this Skill. Do not add API-key management or channel-status redirects, browser reads or new API calls.

scenarios.when: the user requests troubleshooting information from the previous receipt for private support
scenarios.then: Extract only its existing support block. Do not collect logs, configuration, prompts, paths or media, make another request, or upload automatically. Missing support or request_id stays missing. A request ID is not task identity, idempotency or proof of charging; never resubmit to obtain one.

scenarios.when: the user requests a poster with exact text or a background-only edit of the current image
scenarios.then: Preserve the exact requested text and edit scope in the prompt, use the declared image_edit transport for the local reference, and submit one requested design. Do not invent API fields, silently replace the reference with text, split paid tasks, or promise exact visual fidelity.

scenarios.when: the user explicitly asks for historical charges, spending details or an individual generation cost that available results cannot confirm
scenarios.then: Offer https://console.puretokensx.com/usage-logs for the user to inspect by time and model. Do not call balance to derive a charge, infer billing from missing records or task status, guarantee refunds, recover unknown task IDs or automatically append the link to every failure.

scenarios.when: The user asks only for media understanding, OCR, screenshot/video diagnosis, script or prompt writing, or model capability information.
scenarios.then: Do not create a media task. Understanding and writing need no media executor; model capability questions use puretokens-models only. An attachment or model name alone does not authorize generation.

scenarios.when: The user asks to check, resume or retrieve an existing task.
scenarios.then: Route to the matching media Skill and continue only the original task identity; never POST a new task. Preserve existing stop conditions and wait budgets.

scenarios.when: The user supplies a prompt to use verbatim, including prose such as 8K quality, while actual API parameters specify a supported output tier.
scenarios.then: Preserve the exact prompt without translation, quality templates or negative templates. Treat actual API fields separately using the selected profile; do not turn prose into fields. A distinct explicit requirement for actual 8K output must be checked and never silently downgraded.

scenarios.when: A successful HTTP submission response is unreadable, lacks a non-empty top-level identity or contains an unsupported identity type/format.
scenarios.then: Report the corresponding task_response_unreadable, task_id_missing or task_id_invalid local classification, never raw values or invented API error codes. The submission remains unknown; no polling, automatic update, alternate transport or resubmission. Use the existing support.executor_version from the affected client; never substitute the maintainer computer version.

scenarios.when: The original task is confirmed failed without reconciliation or a blocking public error, and a current same-connection authenticated catalog contains an executor-supported candidate satisfying every requirement.
scenarios.then: Explain only this task failure; offer the exact candidate with its compatibility basis, preserve prompt and references, disclose a new task and possible charge, and ask for explicit consent. Do not call submit, invent a global outage, claim health or billing, or change the default model.

scenarios.when: A task is confirmed failed, but only installed profiles, a public catalog or a different/previous connection catalog is available.
scenarios.then: Ask whether to look up compatible models on the current host. Do not name a candidate as accessible or query automatically. If the user agrees to discovery, make one models read only; discovery approval is not generation consent. Explicit model/capability rejection may use its existing one-query diagnostic allowance.

scenarios.when: A returned alternative cannot preserve an image edit, attachment count, video first/last frames, reference roles, output size, duration or required audio.
scenarios.then: Do not present it as a drop-in replacement or silently omit inputs. Explain the specific mismatch and require explicit changed requirements or choose a fully compatible returned candidate. Check both current catalog and selected supported profile; a name is not capability evidence.

scenarios.when: After one exact candidate, all material differences and the possible new charge were explained, the user explicitly says to use it once.
scenarios.then: Create exactly one new submission using the same host and native executor, verbatim explicit prompt and original accessible attachment bytes. Use a new task ID from the response and a separate record; never overwrite or mutate the original record, model, result or default. Do not ask for the same approval again. Report the receipt before follow-up reads.

scenarios.when: The user says continue after several candidates or an unresolved capability change; or agrees only to inspect models.
scenarios.then: Clarify the selected exact model or requirement change without POST. Only a clear response to one fully specified new-task proposal is consent. Never treat catalog lookup permission as creation permission.

scenarios.when: A submission is unknown, times out, has an unreadable/missing ID, or the task is pending, retry-deferred, under reconciliation or has a status-read failure.
scenarios.then: Do not proactively suggest a replacement or read the catalog. Explain uncertainty and retain same-task recovery when possible. A later independent new request after unknown submission requires explicit acknowledgement of possible original completion and duplicate charges; reconciliation remains same-task only. Never reset wait budgets.

scenarios.when: The receipt indicates local host/attachment/network restrictions, authentication, permission, quota, balance, rate limiting, content rejection or user cancellation, even if another field says failed.
scenarios.then: Honor the specific next_action or cancellation. Do not diagnose model outage, look up replacements automatically, suggest changing models as a workaround or bypass content controls.

scenarios.when: Generation completed but content retrieval or native attachment handoff failed.
scenarios.then: Offer only original-task retrieval or reattachment of verified files, not another model. Do not create a new paid task or claim the original model failed.

scenarios.when: The explicitly selected alternative fails or its submission outcome is unknown.
scenarios.then: Return the actual sanitized failure and stop automatic work. Prior consent authorized one new task only, not another model, resubmission or a rotation loop; retain any new and original task IDs.

scenarios.when: The one permitted catalog lookup returns no compatible candidate, denies authorization, or fails.
scenarios.then: Explain that no compatible candidate could be confirmed in this lookup. Do not retry, fall back to a static list, infer global model retirement, change host/connection or POST.

scenarios.when: A model group was renamed in production and a fixture uses a different name.
scenarios.then: Use only the current model-groups receipt group name; never fixture, brand or stale names. Public membership does not prove current-Key permission.

scenarios.when: An exact model has multiple public group mappings.
scenarios.then: Show the returned groups without choosing one or requiring all; preserve existing selections and let the user choose an allowed Switch group.

scenarios.when: The old service has no group_guidance, or mapping is missing, conflicting or unsafe.
scenarios.then: Give generic exact-model group guidance, without guessing from enable_groups or claiming the model is unavailable; do not retry.

scenarios.when: A model permission rejection, a 401 authentication error and an upstream 5xx occur in separate requests.
scenarios.then: Only the explicit model-permission rejection may trigger group guidance. Handle authentication independently. An uncertain 5xx submission keeps same-task recovery and makes no group lookup or new POST.

scenarios.when: The user reports selecting another group or refreshing an already-selected group in Switch.
scenarios.then: Invalidate old connection catalog evidence, preserve existing groups, follow host reload instructions and verify current authenticated visibility only when requested. Applying configuration does not authorize another paid task.

scenarios.when: Switch disables the suggested group for this account or host, including Claude Desktop restrictions.
scenarios.then: Do not bypass host restrictions, change host, expose credentials or promise call support. Explain that public mapping is not account eligibility and stop for user support.
